name: Denver
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Denver: aerospace, energy and cannabis due diligence, asset research and Colorado litigation support.
hero_lede: Denver is the commercial centre of the Rocky Mountain region, with aerospace, energy, financial services and a regulated cannabis market. TDSC scopes investigative consulting from Nashville for matters touching the city, coordinating Colorado-licensed private investigators and the client's counsel where local work is required.
intro: Denver is a consolidated city and county and the capital of Colorado, at the centre of a metropolitan economy that extends along the Front Range to Aurora, Lakewood, Littleton, Broomfield and Boulder. Regional economic development studies have identified aerospace, aviation, bioscience, broadcasting and telecommunications, energy, financial services, health care and software as its main industry clusters, and the region is described as having one of the largest concentrations of private aerospace employment and space activity in the country. Oil and gas companies, renewable energy developers and mining groups have long kept headquarters or regional offices in the city, and Denver International Airport makes it a major national air hub.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Denver because capital moves through it into sectors where counterparty risk is easy to underestimate. Energy and mining ventures raise money for assets located far from the city; aerospace and defence suppliers carry export control and contracting exposures; and Colorado was the first state to legalise recreational cannabis, creating a licensed but federally illegal industry in which ownership, financing and compliance require careful review. Rapid growth in Front Range real estate has also drawn investors who hold property through limited liability companies. Colorado's licensing regime for private investigators and its state privacy law shape how any local fieldwork is planned.

matters.title: Energy and mining counterparty diligence
matters.text: Denver-based oil, gas and mining companies often raise capital for assets in other states or abroad. We review ownership, management histories, litigation, regulatory actions and related entities to test whether operators and promoters are who they claim to be before a client invests, lends or acquires.

matters.title: Aerospace and defence supplier reviews
matters.text: The Front Range supply chain includes prime contractors and many smaller suppliers. We examine ownership, foreign links, debarment and litigation history and reputational issues so clients can identify undisclosed related parties or compliance concerns before teaming, subcontracting or acquisition.

matters.title: Cannabis ownership and financing
matters.text: Colorado's licensed cannabis businesses are often financed through layered entities and management agreements. We map disclosed owners, lenders and affiliates from state licensing and corporate records and public litigation, so investors, lenders and acquirers understand who controls a business and what regulatory history attaches to it.

matters.title: Real estate and LLC ownership
matters.text: Denver residential and commercial property is frequently held through limited liability companies that reveal little about their members. We work from recorded documents, entity filings, tax records and litigation to identify likely beneficial owners and state the strength of each attribution.

matters.title: Asset research for Colorado judgments
matters.text: Creditors enforcing judgments against Denver-based debtors need to know what property, business interests and connected entities exist. We map these from public records so counsel can plan garnishment, liens and other enforcement steps available under Colorado procedure.

local_context.title: Courts sitting in Denver
local_context.text: State civil cases for the City and County of Denver are heard in the Denver District Court, which forms Colorado's Second Judicial District, while the Colorado Supreme Court and Court of Appeals also sit in the city. Federal commercial, securities, fraud and trade secret cases are heard by the United States District Court for the District of Colorado, and the Tenth Circuit Court of Appeals is headquartered in Denver. Federal dockets are available through PACER; counsel decides the forum and we tailor research to its rules.

local_context.title: Colorado private investigator licensing
local_context.text: Colorado did not license private investigators for decades after a 1977 court decision ended an earlier scheme, and the state's regulators long resisted a new one. Licensure became mandatory on 1 June 2015 under Article 160 of Title 12 of the Colorado Revised Statutes, administered by the Department of Regulatory Agencies through its Office of Private Investigator Licensure. There are Level I and Level II licences, both requiring a jurisprudence examination and fingerprint background check. Colorado offers no reciprocity, so TDSC coordinates Colorado-licensed professionals for fieldwork.

local_context.title: Records and registries
local_context.text: Colorado business entities are registered with the Colorado Secretary of State, whose online search shows entity status, registered agent and periodic report filings; members of limited liability companies are generally not shown. Real property documents for Denver are recorded by the Denver Clerk and Recorder, and the city publishes assessment and tax information by parcel. Colorado state court records are not uniformly available online, so document retrieval may require requests to the relevant court.

local_context.title: Privacy and recording rules
local_context.text: Colorado has a comprehensive state consumer privacy statute, the Colorado Privacy Act, enforced by the Attorney General, which applies to many businesses handling Colorado residents' personal data. Colorado law generally permits a participant to record a conversation, but recording of conversations to which the recorder is not a party is prohibited, and federal wiretap law also applies. These rules shape how interviews, surveillance and data collection are planned for Denver matters.

tdsc_approach: TDSC has no office in Denver and works on Denver matters from Nashville. We agree the purpose with the client and its counsel first, whether Colorado or federal litigation, judgment enforcement, an energy, aerospace or cannabis transaction, or an internal review, and scope the research to it. Sources include Colorado Secretary of State filings, Denver property and assessment records, state and federal court dockets, and the licensing and regulatory registers that apply to the sector concerned. Any fieldwork in Colorado is carried out by Colorado-licensed private investigators. Cannabis matters are reviewed carefully given the conflict between state and federal law. Reports identify sources and confidence levels.

faqs.q: Does an investigator need a Colorado licence to work in Denver?
faqs.a: Yes. Since 1 June 2015 Colorado has required private investigators to be licensed by the Department of Regulatory Agencies, with Level I and Level II licences that require a jurisprudence examination and fingerprint background check. Colorado does not recognise licences from other states. TDSC does not hold a Colorado licence and uses licensed Colorado professionals for local work.

faqs.q: Can TDSC review a Colorado cannabis business before investment?
faqs.a: We can carry out due diligence from public sources, including state licensing information, corporate filings, litigation and media, to identify owners, financiers and regulatory history. Because cannabis remains illegal under federal law, the client's counsel should advise on the legal implications of any transaction. We do not advise on whether an investment is lawful.

faqs.q: Where are business disputes heard in Denver?
faqs.a: State business disputes are usually heard in the Denver District Court, part of Colorado's Second Judicial District. Federal cases with interstate or international elements go to the United States District Court for the District of Colorado, and federal appeals to the Tenth Circuit, which sits in Denver. Counsel chooses the forum; we tailor research to its discovery and evidence rules.

faqs.q: How can we find who owns a Denver property held by an LLC?
faqs.a: Recorded documents usually name the entity rather than its members, and Colorado filings generally do not list LLC members. We look for connected records such as mortgages, tax bills, permits, litigation, related entities and public statements that may reveal the people behind it. Where public sources are insufficient, counsel may compel disclosure through legal process.

faqs.q: Do energy or mining investments managed from Denver need checks elsewhere?
faqs.a: Usually. Companies headquartered in Denver often hold assets, leases or concessions in other states or countries. We combine Colorado and federal records with registries and court records in the jurisdictions where the assets sit, coordinating licensed local professionals where needed, so clients see the operator's full ownership and dispute history.
